problems.source_says: Not supported by the body of the paper. The authors' own label for the design is 'quasi-experimental' (p. 2). The form spec reserves quasi_people for non-random assignment such as intact classes. Random assignment appears in one abstract sentence only (p. 1), and no page names a unit, method, or tool of randomization. field_rct is a core code, so it conflicts with the form's own eligibility (criterion 1 unclear, core unclear). Suggested fix: do not code a randomized design class until the paper or the authors say whether students or whole classes were assigned, and how. On the document as it stands, the authors' label points to quasi_people.
problems.quote: To address these research questions, we conducted a quasi-experimental study involving 78 fifth-grade students, divided into control and treatment groups.
problems.locator: p. 2, Introduction, right column (paragraph after RQ4); compare p. 1, Abstract ('randomly assigned')

problems.source_says: Stated only in the abstract and contradicted elsewhere. The Methods say only 'assigned' (p. 4). The Discussion says only 'assigning them to either a control group or a treatment group' (p. 9). The Introduction calls the study quasi-experimental (p. 2), and the Informed consent section calls it 'a non-interventional questionnaire-based study' (p. 14). The only other 'randomized' in the paper refers to the artworks presented for rating, not to assignment (p. 6). So 'yes' records one side of a contradiction as a fact. what_was_assigned reports the abstract and Introduction conflict but omits the p. 9 and p. 14 wording. The arms' n_randomized (39 and 39) depend on this field.

problems.form_value: the two intact classes have 39 students each, the same as the arm sizes, so the arms may be the two classes
problems.source_says: Minor. The size match is weak evidence. With two classes of 39, any balanced split of the 78 students also gives 39 per arm. A coin flip for each student gives exactly 39 and 39 with probability 0.09 (my calculation), and a balanced individual randomization always does. The arm sizes therefore cannot tell individual assignment from class assignment. The real evidence against random assignment of people is the authors' 'quasi-experimental' label and the absence of any unit or procedure. Suggested wording: drop the size argument, or say that it fits both readings.

confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is AI-generated material for the students' own work, not a contrast in whose output is evaluated. In Stage 3 the groups differed in 'the learning resources employed to create PowerPoint presentations': AI-generated artwork (Fig. 3) versus classical artworks (Fig. 4). Each student then painted an anthropomorphic cartoon character by hand, and three teachers rated each student's own painting. role ideas_supplied fits the codebook's 'AI-generated ideas or examples'.

The arm counts match the print. The abstract gives n = 39 per group at assignment, and Tables 1, 3 to 7, and 9 print n = 39 per group. unit other is a fair placeholder, because the paper never says whether students or classes were assigned.

summary: The form codes S1 as a randomized field experiment (randomized yes, field_rct) on the strength of one abstract sentence, but the Introduction calls the study quasi-experimental, the Methods and Discussion say only that students from two classes of 39 were 'assigned', the consent section calls it non-interventional, and no page gives a unit or method of randomization (pp. 1, 2, 4, 9, 14). The treatment (Stable Diffusion example images in the teacher's slides, then hand painting) and the comparison arm (classical cartoon artworks) are coded correctly, so the AI contrast holds, but random assignment of people is not established and criterion 1 stays unclear.
